script: I said no, but her sister's move will destroy my love.. I am in the living room, the couch is all comfy, and my girlfriend just drops the question: "What if X moved in with us for two years while she finishes her master's?" I say, "Absolutely not." She's like, "How would you react if my brother wanted to do that?" I am like, "I hadn't thought of it that way." She and her sister have been living together since they were adults, so to them it's no big deal. Their mom's already planning meals around it, the whole house is set up for two people. Today X walks in, asks the same thing, and I am dead‑set. I try to dodge it, drop the commute angle—120 km, two hours each way, winter trains are a nightmare. I've done that commute for two years, so I know the grind. X says she'll pay rent, contribute to bills. That's not the problem. I didn't sign up for a 30‑year lease of my own privacy. If she lives here, it's going to be constant friction, extra noise, shared space that's never mine. I know the money would help with mortgage payments, but the emotional cost? It's too high. I am scared they'll think I am the bad guy, that my girlfriend's family will snub me for being stubborn. I am not sure if I am overreacting. (I know, right?) The audacity of the whole situation is just too much.
